title: Think Again
mood: A light comes down between the blast and its target, and two old partners face what they kept hidden.

hero.alt: Guinevere stands guard in the smoke, arms crossed and eyes hard, while behind her Vexana kneels on the scorched stone with her staff.

segs.t: Guinevere came over the last rail at the speed of light.
Her wings were thin. Both drones burned at her shoulders.

Below her the platform was black glass and cracked stone. Gray wreckage lay heaped around the middle of it, and there Vexana knelt on one knee. One arm was tucked against her ribs. The other held the staff, and a dark-pink knot burned in its orb.
Her left sleeve was gone to the elbow. The skin under it was burned raw.
Guinevere thought of the machine three streets west, cracked open from the inside.
That was you. You were in it.
Over Vexana stood the Mother Matrix, its violet eyes on her. The plates of its chest split. White light filled the opening.
Now.
Guinevere dropped between them and crossed her arms. Her two drones flung themselves in front of her. The light came down.
It hit the drones first and her second. Light sprayed past her on both sides. Her boots slid back across the stone, and stopped. She held.
Again,
she thought, with that burned arm at her back. Once, in sparring, she had caught Vexana’s wrist and found a bandage under the glove, with blood on it. Vexana had told no one.
“It was mine to carry,” was all she had said.
“There you go again,” Guinevere said through her teeth, “taking on everything by yourself.”
The light thinned and died. The plates closed over the dark in its chest. It would need time to gather again.
Both drones dropped onto the stone, dark and smoking.
On the rubble behind Vexana, something moved. An Ender sprang at her back.
“Ender! Watch out!” Guinevere shouted.
She went past Vexana to meet it. Its chest split as it struck, and she put her fist through the core. It came apart at her boots.
She stood over Vexana with her back to her and her fists up.
“You’re the one who needs my protection!”
Her voice dropped. “Rather than being protected, I choose to fight alongside you.”
The light that sprayed past Guinevere had thrown Vexana flat. She lay on the stone with her hand still on the staff, and looked up at Guinevere’s back.
For one moment the Matrix’s chest had stood open and the core bare. Her whole plan had been made for that moment. Then this back had come down between them.
She had watched it in a hundred fights, from above and behind. The pink ponytail. The red bow, crooked.
Nobody straightened it,
she thought.
Once already today that back had gone past her, close enough to touch.

At the end of their fight over the gap, wings had opened on both of them. Guinevere had flown straight at her with everything she had left. Vexana had leveled the staff at Guinevere’s heart, where every Ender could see it.
At the last meter she turned it aside.
Guinevere’s hand went past her shoulder. It was open. It had never been a fist. The staff went past Guinevere’s ear. They passed side by side, so close their wings brushed.
Vexana had been smiling. For one second they were partners again.
Light burst white where they crossed. No blow had landed on either of them.

media.alt: A memory: a red-gold streak and a violet one rush at each other over the city, Vexana's face close as she flies; then the two sweep past each other side by side, staff and open hand reaching past.

segs.t: Then Guinevere hung in the air with nothing left in her, and fell.
Her voice came up out of the white. “Don’t let me be alone in this world.”
Vexana dived.
Under her breastbone sat the cold point, the Will’s mark. For weeks she had felt its doors open through it, always where the Will sent her, never where she chose. She had never opened one herself.
She pushed at it with everything she was. Something tore.
Under the falling girl a door of the void opened, no wider than her arms.
Guinevere’s hand was still up, open. Vexana’s hand closed on the wrist.
I’m here.
“Hold on to me!”
Guinevere could not hold on. Vexana held on for both of them, and they went into the dark.

media.alt: Vexana, her hair pale and her eyes wide, cries out and throws her hand toward Guinevere, who reaches back for it.
media.credit: Official Guinevere and Vexana interactive drama

segs.t: Cold came up through her, the void’s cold, and no sound at all. Three heartbeats. That was all the door would give.
Then stone. An empty road three streets west, and a low wall. She laid Guinevere down behind it, at the level of the stones, where no eye on the platforms could find her.
Let them see a purge done,
she had thought.
Let it go on trusting me, until it stands whole and close.
It had not worked. At Guinevere’s collar the star blazed. It burned because they were still in sync. Vexana could not stop that, not even to hide her.
Over the bay the crowned head turned west.
Her wings were still open from the dive. She went up over the roofs to where her lead Guard waited, and lit it. Its heart opened, she was inside, and it dropped into the light.
And now she’s done the same for me.
Guinevere turned around.
“Guinevere.” It came out flat. Vexana leaned on the staff and came up onto one knee. “Go. I’ve seen the end that awaits us. There is no other choice...”
Guinevere’s eyes went to the knot in the staff, and stayed there.
“Vexana, if you think I’m going to let you sacrifice yourself for some greater good, think again!”
Her voice went out across the gap. Then she said the rest low.
“This destiny is something the two of us should bear together.”
In the void, on one knee, Vexana had said the other half of that to the dark.
This destiny is mine to bear.
I carried it alone so she would live,
she thought.
And every road I took alone brought her here, in front of the light.
Guinevere crouched and held out her hand, palm up.
Vexana looked at it. She knew that hand. Once, in a courtyard, she had left it held out to nobody.

Under a shaded tree on a clear day, it had waved in the air while Guinevere told a story, her head in Vexana’s lap. Vexana’s palm went over the pink hair, learning how hard to pat. In this memory the sky stayed blue, and she finished the pat.

media.alt: A memory in sunlight: black-haired Vexana sits in the grass under a tree, patting the hair of Guinevere, who lies with her head in her lap, laughing and waving one hand.

segs.t: A corridor after curfew. That same hand in hers, pulling. The lamps on Guinevere’s side, the dark on hers, and her own feet going, against every rule she kept.

Her own room, on one of the last nights she ever slept in it. Her phone in her hand, their photo lit on its screen. On the desk the box stood open, with what that hand had given her: the ticket stubs, the paper fan, the napkin from the doughnut. She laid the pink keychain in with them for the night, and her star beside it.
Beside the photo frame stood the two felt dolls, a pink-haired one and a black-haired one. Under them, in her small square letters, the card waited for next summer.
For Guinevere. Same place, next year.

media.alt: A gloved hand holds a phone whose wallpaper is a photo of the two girls together, above an open box of keepsakes; two felt dolls and a photo frame stand on the desk behind.

segs.t: She had meant to leave all of it behind, and never tell her why.
“Stay with me, Vexana,” said Guinevere.
They were Vexana’s own words, from a street at the dome’s foot, said down to a girl on the ground.
Her burned hand came away from her ribs. She took Guinevere’s hand with it. It hurt. She did not let go.
In her staff the dark-pink knot went out.
Under her right sleeve, her own star burned hot against her wrist.
“You pulled me out of the dark once,” said Vexana.
“So I’m good at it.”
Vexana looked past her, up at the torn star behind the crown. “There may be no going back this time.”
Her mouth moved before she could stop it. She was smiling.
Don’t get used to this,
she had told herself under the fireworks. Now she let it stay.
The star at Guinevere’s collar flared, as bright as it had been that night.
Guinevere’s eyes were wet. She grinned anyway. “As long as we’re together!”
For a moment nothing on the platform moved but the wind.

media.alt: Close on Vexana, her head bowed; she opens her eyes and a small smile comes; then Guinevere turns to her, smiling, a drone rising at her side.

segs.t: Boots rang on the stair that climbed the side of the gap from the seawall.
Fanny came over the rail first, blades out. Layla came behind her, then Ruby and Angela. On the steps below them gray wreckage lay all the way down to the water.
Fanny saw the robe and the black staff. Her blades stayed up, on Vexana.
Layla looked at the burned arm, then at the scorched stone. “So that’s who climbed out.” Her cannon came down. “It’s not a trap. Nobody burns their own arm for a trap.”
Guinevere stood, still holding Vexana’s hand, and pulled her up with it. Vexana’s ribs caught. She stayed up.
“This morning I went alone so none of you would walk into a trap meant for me,” said Guinevere. She looked at each of them. “I can’t do this alone. Cover us.”
Behind the crown, white light was gathering again.
Guinevere turned to face it. “Aspirants! Today, our light shall pierce the Singularity!”
“Hope never dies!”
Vexana heard it come out of her own mouth.
Not long ago I told her hope was an illusion.
“The Aspirants always stand united!”
Everyone said it. Fanny said it too, with her blades still raised.
On the stone the two dark drones shivered. Smoke still trailing, they lifted and found Guinevere’s shoulders.
Wings opened on both girls, thin and bright. Then they rose side by side toward the crowned head, one light gold and one violet.
